complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: 컴포넌트 기반 정비 및 더미 데이터 준비
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break down component setup into: (1) installing 6 shadcn/ui components via CLI, (2) creating lib/dummy-links.ts with 10+ diverse Link objects covering all edge cases (thumbnail presence, tag count variations, read/favorite states), (3) implementing lib/format-utils.ts with formatRelativeTime, extractDomain, and parseTags functions with proper edge case handling, (4) updating next.config.ts for external image domains or documenting the decision to use plain img tags instead of next/image.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This is a straightforward setup task with clear deliverables. The codebase already has shadcn/ui configured (components.json exists, 7 components installed). Installing 6 more components is CLI work. Creating dummy data and utility functions are simple TypeScript tasks. No complex business logic or async operations. The only decision point is next/image configuration, but the task provides both options. Low complexity despite multiple steps because each step is independent and well-defined.

Very simple task. app/page.tsx already exists with auth redirect logic in place. The task just requires replacing the current content with the landing page template provided in the details section. No database interaction, no complex state management, minimal styling. The redirect logic (if user → /links) is already implemented. Responsive design using Tailwind is straightforward. This is essentially a copy-paste task with minor adjustments. No subtasks needed—can be completed in one implementation step.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: 링크 목록 페이지 UI 구현 (더미 데이터)
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Divide into: (1) Create LinkCard component with thumbnail/title/domain/tags/memo display and action buttons (read/favorite/delete) with proper event handling to prevent card click propagation, (2) Create SearchFilterBar component UI shell (no logic, just input/select/button elements), (3) Create LinkListSkeleton component for loading states, (4) Update app/links/page.tsx to render grid layout with dummy data from lib/dummy-links.ts, handle empty state, and integrate all components, (5) Test responsive grid (1/2/3 columns) and dark mode appearance.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate complexity with multiple interconnected components. Requires creating 3 new components (LinkCard, SearchFilterBar, LinkListSkeleton) plus updating the existing /links page. The LinkCard component has non-trivial logic: preventing button clicks from triggering card navigation (event.stopPropagation), handling Image component with fallback, line-clamping text. Grid layout with responsive breakpoints needs testing. Integration of multiple UI elements requires careful composition. Not high complexity because there's no server interaction yet (dummy data only), but substantial front-end work across multiple files.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: 링크 저장 모달 UI 구현 (더미 데이터)
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Structure as: (1) Create SaveLinkDialog component skeleton with Dialog/DialogContent/DialogHeader/DialogFooter structure, (2) Implement URL input section with validation and preview button, including error state display, (3) Implement metadata preview area with three distinct states (loading skeleton, success preview with thumbnail/title/description, failed state with manual title input), (4) Implement tags input with real-time badge preview using parseTags utility and memo textarea, (5) Wire up form submission logic (dummy for now) and integrate dialog trigger into app/links/page.tsx, ensuring modal opens/closes correctly and is responsive on mobile.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Higher complexity due to complex state management for the modal. The component has multiple UI states (initial, loading metadata, metadata success, metadata failure), conditional rendering logic, and form validation. The tag parsing with real-time badge preview requires controlled input handling. The details section shows a substantial component (~150+ lines) with nested conditionals. Converting app/links/page.tsx to a client component to manage dialog state adds integration complexity. The modal must handle Esc key, scrollability on mobile, and focus management. While still UI-only (no real API calls), the state machine complexity and multiple user interaction flows justify a moderate-high score.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: links 테이블 및 데이터 액세스 레이어 구축
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break into: (1) Apply Supabase migration via mcp__supabase__apply_migration to create links table with all fields, FK to auth.users, and default values, (2) Add RLS policies (enable RLS, create 4 policies for select/insert/update/delete restricted to auth.uid() = user_id), (3) Create performance indexes (user_id, created_at DESC, GIN on tags array), (4) Generate TypeScript types using mcp__supabase__generate_typescript_types and save to types/database.types.ts, (5) Align types/link.ts interface with generated types to ensure consistency, (6) Implement lib/queries/links.ts with getLinks function including basic filter support (search, tags, read status, favorite), and test RLS with 2 test users to verify isolation.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: This is the first real database work and a critical foundation task. Involves multiple technologies: Supabase migrations, PostgreSQL (including array columns and GIN indexes), RLS policies (4 separate policies with correct auth.uid() logic), TypeScript type generation, and query function implementation. The getLinks function already includes complex filter logic (OR for search, array overlap for tags). RLS testing requires creating multiple test accounts and verifying data isolation, which is time-consuming. Type alignment between generated types and manual interfaces can be tricky. Mistakes here will cascade to all future tasks. The migration is irreversible in production. High complexity justified by the multi-layered nature of the work and critical importance.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Divide into: (1) Install zod and sonner dependencies, (2) Create lib/actions/links.ts with createLink Server Action including zod schema validation, user authentication check, Supabase insert, and revalidatePath, (3) Implement deleteLink Server Action with RLS backup check, (4) Update components/save-link-dialog.tsx to replace dummy save with actual createLink call, handle pending state (disable button), and show toast notifications, (5) Update components/link-card.tsx to add AlertDialog for delete confirmation and wire up deleteLink action, (6) Convert app/links/page.tsx from dummy data to real getLinks() call, handle loading/error states with proper Suspense boundaries, (7) Add Toaster to app/layout.tsx and run full E2E test (save with validation errors, save success, delete with confirmation, empty state) using Playwright MCP.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: High complexity marking the transition from UI mockups to fully functional backend-connected features. Introduces multiple new concepts: Server Actions (which require careful handling in Next.js 15), zod validation schemas, revalidatePath for cache invalidation, toast notifications (sonner), optimistic UI patterns. The task requires modifying 5+ files across different layers (actions, components, pages, layout). Converting the page from dummy data to server component data fetching requires understanding React 19 Server Components and Suspense. The AlertDialog integration for delete adds another layer. The Playwright MCP testing requirement means the implementation must be fully functional end-to-end. Error handling for network failures, duplicate submissions, and validation errors adds substantial code paths. This is where the app becomes real.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Structure as: (1) Install open-graph-scraper dependency, (2) Create lib/metadata.ts with fetchLinkMetadata function including URL validation, protocol/hostname checks for SSRF protection (block localhost/127.0.0.1/169.254.169.254), timeout handling with Promise.race, and OG tag parsing from ogs library result, (3) Create lib/actions/metadata.ts with fetchMetadataAction Server Action wrapper, (4) Update components/save-link-dialog.tsx to call fetchMetadataAction on preview button click, handle loading/success/error states with conditional rendering of preview area vs manual input, (5) Update next.config.ts to add images.remotePatterns configuration for external thumbnails (or document decision to use img tag), (6) Test with Playwright MCP covering both successful OG fetch (e.g., github.com) and failed cases (e.g., example.com), plus SSRF protection (localhost URLs should be rejected).
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: High complexity due to security concerns and external API interaction. The task introduces asynchronous operations with real network requests, which can fail in many ways (timeout, malformed HTML, missing OG tags, network errors). SSRF protection is a security requirement that must be implemented correctly—blocking internal IPs, validating protocols. The Promise.race timeout pattern is non-trivial. Parsing OG tags from the ogs library response requires understanding its data structure. The UI must handle three distinct states (loading, success with preview, failure with manual fallback), which requires careful state management in the dialog component. Testing requires actual URLs and network conditions. The next/image configuration decision adds another consideration. Security-sensitive code with multiple failure modes justifies high complexity.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: F003 태그 및 F004 메모 저장 연동
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break into: (1) Enhance lib/format-utils.ts parseTags function with normalization (lowercase, trim, 50-char max length, deduplication), (2) Update components/save-link-dialog.tsx to use parseTags before submitting to createLink and show real-time tag badge preview as user types, (3) Create lib/queries/tags.ts with getUserTags function that queries links table, flattens tags arrays, deduplicates, and sorts, (4) Update components/search-filter-bar.tsx (or make it server component) to fetch and display user's tags in the dropdown, (5) Add tag badge click handler in components/link-card.tsx that updates URL params to filter by clicked tag, and update app/links/page.tsx to read tag from URL params and pass to getLinks filter.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate complexity involving data transformation and UI state synchronization. The parseTags normalization logic requires careful handling of edge cases (empty strings, whitespace, duplicates, case sensitivity). The getUserTags function involves array flattening from a SQL query result, which is straightforward but requires understanding PostgreSQL array columns. The tag dropdown population requires deciding between server component (fetch in RSC) vs client component (pass as prop), each with tradeoffs. The tag badge click → URL param → filter flow introduces state management via URL params, which is the recommended approach for shareable/back-button-compatible filtering. Coordinating between multiple components (dialog, card, filter bar, page) requires careful prop threading. Not high complexity because it's mostly data flow without complex algorithms, but substantial integration work.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: F005 읽음 및 F006 즐겨찾기 토글 구현
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Divide into: (1) Add toggleRead and toggleFavorite Server Actions to lib/actions/links.ts with user authentication check, current state parameter, Supabase update with negated state, and revalidatePath, (2) Create LinkList client component wrapper in app/links/page.tsx using useOptimistic hook to manage optimistic updates with proper state shape ({ id, field, value }), (3) Implement handleToggleRead and handleToggleFavorite functions that update optimistic state immediately, call the action, and show error toast on failure, (4) Update components/link-card.tsx visual styling to differentiate read (green icon/badge) vs unread, favorite (filled red heart) vs not favorite (outline), and add aria-label to buttons for accessibility, (5) Test with Playwright MCP covering toggle actions, state persistence across refresh, visual distinction, and error recovery (offline mode → toast → state rollback).
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate-high complexity introducing optimistic updates, a React 19 pattern that's powerful but tricky to implement correctly. The useOptimistic hook requires understanding its reducer-like API and how to structure the update shape. The Server Actions are straightforward (simple UPDATE queries), but the client-side coordination is non-trivial. Converting the page to use a client component wrapper while maintaining server-rendered initial data requires careful Next.js architecture. Error handling for optimistic updates is critical—the UI must roll back to the correct state on failure, which requires testing with offline mode. Visual styling for read/favorite states adds more work. ARIA labels for accessibility add another dimension. The Playwright test must verify both immediate UI updates (optimistic) and persisted state (after refresh), which is more complex than previous tests. The multi-state nature (4 combinations: read/unread × favorite/not) increases test surface area.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Structure as: (1) Enhance lib/queries/links.ts getLinks function to support full LinkFilter interface with text search across title/memo/tags (using Postgres ilike and array operators), tag array intersection (contains), read status (eq true/false), and favorite (eq true), (2) Install use-debounce dependency, (3) Convert components/search-filter-bar.tsx to client component with useRouter, useSearchParams, and useTransition for navigation, (4) Implement debounced search input with useDebouncedCallback (500ms), (5) Implement select dropdowns for tags and read status, favorite toggle button, and reset button that clears all params, (6) Update app/links/page.tsx to read all searchParams, construct LinkFilter object, pass to getLinks, and pass availableTags to SearchFilterBar, (7) Add empty search result state UI and test full filter combinations with Playwright MCP (search + tag + read + favorite, URL persistence, back button, filter reset).
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: High complexity due to the combination of advanced filtering logic, URL state management, and debounced input handling. The getLinks query enhancement requires understanding Postgres full-text search operators (ilike, cs.{}, contains, overlaps) and how to combine multiple filters with AND logic. The client-side implementation involves multiple React hooks (useRouter, useSearchParams, useTransition) and a third-party hook (useDebouncedCallback) that must work together correctly. URL parameter synchronization is tricky—parameters must be added/removed without causing unnecessary navigation, and the scroll position should be preserved. The updateParams function requires careful logic to handle null/empty/all values correctly. The filter combination creates a large state space (4 filter dimensions) that must all work together. Testing requires verifying URL updates, filter accuracy, debounce behavior, and browser back/forward button behavior. The interaction between server component (page reading searchParams) and client component (filter bar updating params) adds architectural complexity. This is one of the most complex features because it touches all layers and has many interaction modes.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Organize as: (1) Create tests/e2e-scenarios.md documenting all test scenarios, (2) Run full user journey E2E test with Playwright MCP (signup → login → empty state → save with metadata → save with fallback → tag/memo → search/filter → toggle → delete → logout), (3) Test edge cases (300-char title, long URL, no tags, no memo, unicode/emoji search, broken thumbnail, invalid image URL), (4) Test error scenarios (metadata timeout, Server Action failure simulation, concurrent updates in 2 tabs, invalid URL formats, network failures), (5) Test security and accessibility (non-auth access redirects, RLS enforcement with 2 users, XSS in search input, SQL injection attempts, keyboard navigation, focus management, screen reader labels, page load performance with 100+ links).
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate complexity but very time-consuming. This is primarily a QA/testing task rather than development. The complexity comes from the breadth of testing required—16 specific test items listed in the testStrategy. While each individual test is straightforward, coordinating them all, documenting results, and handling regressions is substantial work. Testing concurrent updates (2 tabs) requires browser-specific setup. Security testing (XSS, SQL injection) requires crafting malicious inputs. Performance testing with 100+ links requires data seeding. Accessibility testing requires knowledge of WCAG standards and screen reader usage. The task explicitly states 'Document all failures in respective task files for regression fixes,' which means regressions could trigger rework on previous tasks. Not higher complexity because it's mostly manual testing (or Playwright scripting) rather than coding, but the thoroughness required and potential for discovery of issues justifies moderate score. No subtasks by default, but organizing into categories makes it manageable.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: 사용자 경험 마감 및 접근성 정리
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Divide into: (1) Create error boundaries (app/links/loading.tsx, app/links/error.tsx, app/error.tsx) with proper fallback UI and reset functionality, (2) Conduct responsive design audit across all pages at 375px/768px/1440px breakpoints, verify modal scrollability on mobile, check touch target sizes (min 44x44px), and fix any layout issues, (3) Conduct dark mode audit across all pages, verify WCAG AA contrast ratios, check card border visibility, ensure focus states are visible in dark mode, (4) Improve keyboard accessibility by adding focus trap to SaveLinkDialog (@radix-ui/react-focus-scope), verifying Tab order, ensuring Esc closes modals, testing all interactions without mouse, (5) Update app/layout.tsx metadata (title, description, openGraph) and add favicons (app/favicon.ico, app/icon.png, app/apple-icon.png) with LinkLink branding.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate complexity covering multiple polish and accessibility tasks. Creating error boundaries is straightforward (the task provides templates), but proper error logging and reset functionality requires thought. The responsive design audit is manual but thorough—testing at 3 breakpoints across 6+ pages/modals and fixing issues found. Dark mode audit requires checking contrast ratios (tools available but manual process) and potentially adjusting color values. Keyboard accessibility improvements require understanding focus management—the focus trap requires installing and configuring @radix-ui/react-focus-scope, and ensuring logical Tab order may require restructuring HTML. Testing keyboard-only navigation across the entire app is time-consuming. Favicon creation requires image assets (design work or finding suitable icons). While no single item is very complex, the breadth of the task (error handling, responsive, dark mode, a11y, metadata) and the manual testing/fixing cycles add up. This is typical pre-launch polish work—important but less technically complex than core features.

complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Structure as: (1) Create .env.example documenting all required environment variables (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY), (2) Connect GitHub repo to Vercel, configure environment variables in dashboard, deploy main branch, and note production URL, (3) Update Supabase Auth configuration in dashboard to add production callback/confirm URLs and update site URL, (4) Verify production build by checking logs, testing all pages for 500 errors, checking browser console for client errors, and confirming HTTPS/SSL works, (5) Run smoke tests in production (manual or Playwright MCP) covering full user journey (signup, login, save, search, toggle, delete, logout), (6) Test OG metadata edge cases in production (login-required pages, SNS private posts, slow sites with timeout) and document findings in PRD '[확인 필요]' section with verdict on whether manual fallback is sufficient.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate-high complexity due to deployment configuration and production validation. While Vercel deployment is generally smooth (especially with Next.js), the multi-step process has potential failure points: environment variable misconfig can break auth entirely, Supabase callback URL mismatch prevents login, SSL issues can block API calls. The task requires navigating two different admin dashboards (Vercel, Supabase) and ensuring they're in sync. Smoke testing in production is critical but time-consuming—must run all E2E tests again in production environment to catch environment-specific issues (CORS, API limits, cold starts). The OG metadata edge case testing is particularly complex because it requires finding real URLs that represent each failure mode (login-required, private posts, slow sites) and verifying the behavior in production. The requirement to update PRD documentation based on findings adds another step. Potential for issues to emerge only in production (e.g., serverless function timeouts, rate limits) that require debugging without local environment. The optional custom domain setup adds more complexity if pursued. This is a critical gate before launch—mistakes here mean production outages.

complexityAnalysis.taskTitle: profiles 테이블 및 사용자 데이터 동기화 트리거 마이그레이션 적용
complexityAnalysis.expansionPrompt: Break into: (1) Apply Supabase migration via mcp__supabase__apply_migration executing the PROFILES_TABLE_DDL from types/database.ts, including the profiles table creation, updated_at trigger function and trigger, handle_new_user() SECURITY DEFINER trigger reading raw_user_meta_data, and RLS enablement with own-row policies (no anon grant), (2) Verify migration success and run alongside Task 8's links migration in the same session so both schema changes land together, (3) Regenerate Supabase types using mcp__supabase__generate_typescript_types, save to types/database.types.ts, and ensure types/profile.ts stays consistent with generated schema, (4) Test trigger behavior by signing up a new test user and verifying auto-created profiles row, test updated_at trigger by updating a profile row, and verify RLS with 2 test users to confirm isolation.
complexityAnalysis.reasoning: Moderate-high complexity due to PostgreSQL trigger implementation and testing requirements. The migration itself is drafted (in types/database.ts from Task 18), but applying it correctly requires understanding: trigger functions (handle_profiles_updated_at, handle_new_user), SECURITY DEFINER implications (runs with elevated privileges), raw_user_meta_data JSON extraction (->>, which can be null), and CASCADE behavior. The handle_new_user() trigger reads from auth.users.raw_user_meta_data, which won't have data initially (signup form doesn't collect display_name/avatar_url per the codebase review), so the trigger will insert nulls—this is expected but must be verified. Coordinating this migration with Task 8's links migration 'in the same session' adds synchronization complexity—both must succeed or fail together. Type regeneration and alignment is straightforward but critical (mismatched types break the build). RLS testing with 2 users requires creating test accounts and verifying one user can't access another's profile. Trigger testing requires actual signup flow (not just SQL inserts) to verify auth.users insert triggers profile creation. This is infrastructure work that's foundational but less visible than features, with correctness being critical.
